items.title: Hal Galper interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 27, 2022
items.q: David Baker said, “You don’t learn anything playing with your peers.”

ctx.x: Well said. That’s a good point. You can’t justify a four year jazz program by just or focusing on the rhythm I don’t think. The pedagogy won’t sustain.

That speaks to the system then. I have my own — I came up with my own system. What they did is they destroyed it. The white people who run the academia there destroyed music. Destroyed jazz. You’ve got these older white men making all these decisions about music that really comes from a black culture. And this is a really — I’m on my soapbox on this because traditionally people talk about information and process. Right? You’ve got to learn the information and then you’ve got to learn how to use it. All right? ©…

So you learn the information in school, you learn how to use it in the apprenticeship system. All right? That’s the only place to learn is the apprenticeship system. You have to play the stuff. You have to try it out and you have to be playing with a master. You can’t — David Baker said, “You don’t learn anything playing with your peers.” You have to play — and all the masters that I played with, apprenticed with, they all had awe. They were awesome. And if they told you do something you stood up and saluted and…
